The paper titled "Allo-AVA: A Large-Scale Multimodal Conversational AI Dataset for Allocentric Avatar Gesture Animation" presents a significant advancement in the field of conversational AI by introducing a comprehensive dataset named Allo-AVA, which is aimed at improving avatar animations in virtual environments. The authors, Saif Punjwani and Larry Heck from Georgia Institute of Technology, discuss the critical challenges faced in creating life-like avatar animations, including the scarcity of high-quality, multimodal training data that accurately captures the intricate synchronization of speech, facial expressions, and body movements characteristic of natural communication. It features rich multimedia elements, including audio tracks, transcripts, and about 135 billion extracted keypoints that represent detailed body poses across millions of video frames. ### Methodology The methodology for constructing the Allo-AVA dataset is systematic and involves multiple stages: The authors utilized a combination of search queries targeting allocentric gestures and communication to extract relevant videos from YouTube, applying strict filters to ensure quality and relevance—specifying factors like minimum view counts, video duration, and language. This model leverages the richness of the Allo-AVA dataset, outperforming existing gesture generation models across several metrics, such as Fréchet Gesture Distance (FGD), Fréchet Inception Distance (FID), and Average Pairwise Distance (APD) reflecting gesture diversity and quality. results.title: Reproducibility in Software Engineering | French Reproducible Research Network
results.content: # Reproducibility in Software Engineering. This concept has been extended to computer science, focusing on the ability to recreate identical software artefacts. However, the importance of reproducibility in software engineering is often overlooked, leading to challenges in the validation, security, and reliability of software products. This master’s thesis aims to investigate the current state of reproducibility in software engineering, exploring both the barriers and potential solutions to making software more reproducible and raising awareness. To tackle these issues, I propose an empirical comparison of tools facilitating software reproducibility. To provide a comprehensive assessment of reproducibility in software engineering, this study adopts a methodology that involves a hands-on evaluation of four different methods and tools. Through a systematic evaluation of these tools, this research seeks to determine their effectiveness in establishing and maintaining identical software environments and builds. This study contributes to academic knowledge and offers practical insights that could influence future software development protocols and standards. “Reproducibility in Software Engineering”, *Master’s Thesis in Computer Science*, Dellaiera, Pol, https://zenodo.org/records/12666899.
